sentences.text: Strong and colleagues named the genus Gavialimimus in 2020 based on an articulated skull and fragmentary postcrania found in the Ouled Abdoun Basin.
A 4-meter long specimen of Gavialimimus was found inside the stomach contents of a 6.5 to 7-meter long Prognathodon kianda in Angola.
Gut contents analysis suggests that Prognathodon kianda preferred to eat the heads of other mosasaurs, including Gavialimimus.
Gavialimimus belongs to the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
Phylogenetic analyses place Gavialimimus within the clade Selmasaurini, which also includes Goronyosaurus and Selmasaurus.
Gavialimimus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
This animal lived in Morocco and possibly Angola during this time.
Evidence suggests that larger prognathodontine mosasaurs preyed upon Gavialimimus.
